record_identity.title: ContextEcho agentic-coding research released fabricated and misattributed bibliography entries

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Original ContextEcho research paper and subsequent third version with citation discrepancies identified in November 2026
incident_identity.date_basis: The artefact was first public on 2026-05-22; 4 November 2026 is the date of external discovery and scrutiny, not a claim of continuous writing or publication up to that day. For revised papers each later version is part of the same publication occurrence.

summary: On 22 May 2026, researchers affiliated with Accenture's Center for Advanced AI released ContextEcho, an arXiv research preprint on assistant persona drift in long coding sessions. The original version contained bibliographic entries that misrepresented other research. For example, reference 67 attributed a supposed 'Persona-driven sycophancy' paper to arXiv:2402.08471, an identifier that belongs to an unrelated physics article. A 4 November GPTZero investigation reported seven seriously incorrect references out of 102 assessed. The research preprint was revised on 27 August and 29 October, but the source investigation does not establish what errors remain in each version. The publication-stage source fidelity problem is observable; any use of generative AI to compose particular references is inferred, not demonstrated by authoring traces or author admissions.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: arXiv's original version history fixes the publication date as 22 May 2026. In its own v1 HTML reference list the authors present an alleged LLM sycophancy study under arXiv identifier 2402.08471, while that identifier resolves to an unrelated physics publication. GPTZero's 4 November audit independently reports seven such materially inaccurate bibliographic entries out of 102 and says its high AI-detector score is circumstantial rather than conclusive evidence of AI-generated citations. The later 29 October revision updates the research and bibliography, so unverified claims that every original defect persisted into every later version are excluded. The arXiv authors list affiliations, not an official Accenture institutional report.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The assessed conduct is the release and research-stage reliance on specific unfaithful citations and claims within ContextEcho. The suspected participating generative-AI research/drafting component has not been identified; public output and independently checkable source discrepancies nevertheless show material below the epistemic assurance appropriate for publication. The cause remains disputed or unverified: the resulting provisional Epistemic Reliance Calibration failure applies to the observable generated/retrieved/transformed/synthesised epistemic artefact as it was supplied for scholarly or policy reliance, not an assertion that any identified LLM generated the error. The authors and publishing bodies are accountable for publication, but the available evidence does not assign the erroneous words to a specific person, model or tool. External GPTZero detection is not the assessed AI platform.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This occurrence illustrates the separation between observable deficient epistemic assurance and unknown internal generative-system topology. Professional reliance requires source verification proportionate to publication-stage evidentiary use even where model trace and authorship details are unavailable. The correction or investigator response can be recorded without transferring its actions to the assessed synthetic component.
assessment_boundaries: Accenture researchers' affiliations and emails do not make this arXiv preprint a formal Accenture corporate publication.

A flawed reference and source-ID mismatch are directly observable in the original version. The seven-of-102 figure is attributed to GPTZero's investigation rather than a comprehensive independent audit.
No published drafting transcript, prompt, specific model identity, or author admission proves that a generative system generated reference 67.
The later version history must be assessed as separate revisions of the same publication, not different platform incidents or proof of author wrongdoing.
No downstream correction demand, citation uptake, demonstrable reputational injury or loss beyond the reported deficient published bibliography has been verified.
The underlying research results about persona drift are not demonstrated false merely because references are incorrect.
Not every citation issue is a fabricated source; author, title, venue and identifier discrepancies have different evidentiary weight.
Any FC-062 result is expressly provisional pending further source evidence of generative AI participation, not a legal or scholarly finding of deliberate deception.
Publication/author workflow uncertainty is reported as a limitation, not falsely resolved through hypothetical prompts or model selection.
No independently acting defender AI is assessed in this incident; post-publication investigations and corrections are source/outcome context.
